note: Lifted NMOP model. RFC 9940 separates what legacy conflates: event, anomaly, symptom, fault, alarm (a State), problem (a State), cause, incident; plus the anomaly-semantics annotations (concern, confidence). Many concepts have no legacy equivalent (the legacy alarm swallows them). Same field conventions as the legacy model.

concepts.label: resource
concepts.gloss: a resource whose characteristics are observed

concepts.label: event
concepts.gloss: the variation in the value of a characteristic of a resource at a distinct moment in time (RFC 9940)
concepts.example: a pre-FEC BER sample at t0

concepts.label: anomaly
concepts.gloss: an unusual or unexpected event or pattern that DEVIATES from normal, expected behaviour (RFC 9940) — a deviation, NOT by definition undesirable; it may be perfectly benign
concepts.example: a rising pre-FEC BER trend on lambda1 that may be benign during maintenance

concepts.label: symptom
concepts.gloss: an observable value/state/event considered an indication of a problem or potential problem (RFC 9940)
concepts.example: the BER anomaly taken as a symptom of degradation

concepts.label: fault
concepts.gloss: an occurrence (event or change) that is not desired/required, as it may indicate a current or future undesired state (RFC 9940)

concepts.label: alarm
concepts.gloss: an undesirable STATE in a resource that requires corrective action — a state in its own right (RFC 9940)
concepts.example: the signal-degrade alarm state on lambda1

concepts.label: problem
concepts.gloss: a state that is undesirable and that may require remedial action (RFC 9940)

concepts.label: cause
concepts.gloss: the events, established by CORRELATION, that gave rise to a fault or problem (RFC 9940) — derived, not a static code
concepts.example: the optical BER symptom found to be the root of the IP loss

concepts.label: incident
concepts.gloss: an undesired occurrence such as interruption, degradation or below-target performance of a service, formed by correlating symptoms (RFC 9940 / incident-yang)
concepts.example: one incident correlating the optical and IP symptoms

concepts.label: concern-score
concepts.gloss: a DYNAMIC concern score (0-100) reflecting the current degree of concern given context (anomaly-semantics) — recomputed, not a fixed label
concepts.example: concern 78 for the BER trend now

concepts.label: confidence-score
concepts.gloss: a confidence score (0-100): the detector's confidence in the anomaly classification (anomaly-semantics)
